parts.problem_md:
Packet switching is used to transmit the data packets across the network.

**Identify **the device that controls which path is taken by each data packet.
parts.solution_md:
The device that controls which path is taken by each data packet is:

- Router **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
A user wants to connect their computer to a network.

A dynamic internet protocol (IP) address is allocated to the computer when it is connected to the network.

**Describe **what is meant by a **dynamic IP address**.
parts.solution_md:
A dynamic IP address is described as:

- It can be used to** uniquely identify** a device (on a network) **[1 mark]**
- It can change **[1 mark]**
- Each time the device is connected to the network **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
A web server has an internet protocol (IP) address.

**Give three **characteristics of an **IP address**.
parts.solution_md:
Characteristics of an IP address include:

Any **three **of the following:

- consists of values between 0–255 / 0–FFF **[1 mark]**
- values are separated by full stops / colons **[1 mark]**
- it is a unique address **[1 mark]**
- can be static or dynamic (accept: static, dynamic) **[1 mark]**
- can be public or private (accept: public, private) **[1 mark]**
- can be IPv4 / have four groups of digits **[1 mark]**
- can be IPv6 / have eight groups of digits / uses hexadecimal **[1 mark]**
- in IPv6 :: can replace groups of zeros **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Give three distinct characteristics of the address itself, not vague facts like how it is assigned

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

- Accept a stated unique serial number/ID as satisfying the uniqueness point.
- Accept "represented in hexadecimal" for a mark.
- Do not accept MAC address length (e.g. "8 byte", "48 bits").

A school network has several computers.

Each computer in the network has a media access control (MAC) address.

Hexadecimal is used for MAC addresses. Part of a MAC address is given.

**97–5C–E1 **

Each pair of digits is stored as binary in an 8-bit register.

**Describe **what is meant by a **MAC address**.
parts.solution_md:
A MAC address is described as:

Any **four **of the following:

- used to identify a device **[1 mark]**
- it is a unique (address) **[1 mark]** *accept stating the device's serial number is unique*
- it is a static address **OR** it does not change **[1 mark]**
- it is set by the manufacturer **[1 mark]**
- the first part is the manufacturer ID / number / identifies the manufacturer **[1 mark]**
- the second part is the serial number / ID **[1 mark]**
- it is represented in hexadecimal **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> With 4 marks on offer, make sure you give four clearly distinct points rather than repeating one idea.
> 
> Don't forget the two-part structure: the first part is the manufacturer ID and the second part is the serial number.
> 
> State clearly that a MAC address is used to identify a device, don't just describe communication on a network.

parts.problem_md:
A user wants to connect their computer to a network.

**Identify **the component in the computer that is needed to access a network
parts.solution_md:
The component needed to access a network is:

- Network interface card/controller **OR** NIC **OR** WNIC **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md: **Identify **the type of address that is allocated to the component by the manufacturer, which is used to uniquely identify the device.
parts.solution_md:
The type of address used to uniquely identify the device is:

- Media access control/MAC address **OR **MAC **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
A dynamic internet protocol (IP) address is allocated to the computer when it is connected to the network.

**Identify **the device on the network that can connect multiple devices and automatically assign them an IP address.
parts.solution_md:
The device on the network that can automatically assign IP addresses is the:

- Router **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

- Accept "serial number" for "contains the serial code/number".
- Accept "manufacturer ID" for "contains the manufacturer ID/code/number".

Many devices have a Media Access Control (MAC) address.

**Give three **features of a MAC address.
parts.solution_md:
Examples of features of a MAC address include:

Any **three **of the following:

- It is a unique address **[1 mark]**
- It is assigned by the manufacturer **[1 mark]**
- It can be used to identify a device **[1 mark]**
- It contains the manufacturer ID/code/number **[1 mark]**
- It contains the serial code/number **[1 mark]**
- It is written in hexadecimal **[1 mark]**
- It has 6 bytes/48 bits/6 pairs of digits **[1 mark]**
- Does not (usually) change **OR** static **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Describe a property of the MAC address itself, not related hardware like a NIC

parts.problem_md:
A web server has an internet protocol (IP) address.

**Identify** the network component that uses the IP address to send data only to its correct destination.
parts.solution_md:
The network component that uses the IP address to send data is:

- Router **[1 mark]**
